replies.text: I need to call get-review-context first to get the submission token, then submit the threat model.

Since I cannot call the submit-threat-model action (it's not available in my current environment), I'm outputting the threat model JSON object as instructed:

```json
{
  "schema": "redline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-02",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["product page renderer", "comment input form", "comment storage", "rich text parser", "admin moderation interface"],
    "dataStores": ["comments database"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["customer input", "public internet", "admin interface"],
    "dataClasses": [],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Stored XSS through malicious HTML in rich-text comments",
      "scenario": "Attacker posts comment containing script tags or event handlers disguised as formatting. When any visitor views the product page, the malicious script executes in their browser, stealing session cookies or performing actions as that user.",
      "component": "rich text parser",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.3", "V14.4.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could embed malicious code in a comment that runs when anyone views the page, letting them steal accounts or perform actions as other users.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Sanitize rich-text input to prevent script execution",
        "given": "a customer submits a comment with rich-text formatting",
        "when": "the comment contains HTML tags or attributes",
        "then": "strip or escape all potentially dangerous tags (script, iframe, object, embed) and event handlers (onclick, onerror) before storage"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Admin session hijacking via XSS in moderation interface",
      "scenario": "Attacker posts comment with XSS payload. When moderator views it in the admin interface to review/delete, the script steals the moderator's session token, granting attacker admin access to delete any comments or potentially access other admin functions.",
      "component": "admin moderation interface",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen" },
        { "quote": "Comments are stored in the comments database and rendered" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.3", "V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79", "CWE-384"],
      "plainLanguage": "Malicious code in a comment could steal a moderator's login when they try to review it, giving the attacker moderator powers.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Apply strict output encoding in admin interfaces",
        "given": "a moderator views comments in the admin moderation screen",
        "when": "comments contain user-provided rich text",
        "then": "apply context-aware output encoding and render in sandboxed iframe with restricted CSP"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Session token theft via XSS accessing document.cookie",
      "scenario": "Successful XSS payload reads document.cookie containing session token and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled server. Attacker uses stolen token to impersonate victim user or moderator, accessing their account and data.",
      "component": "product page renderer",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" },
        { "quote": "rendered for every visitor" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V3.4.1", "V3.4.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79", "CWE-539"],
      "plainLanguage": "If an attacker gets malicious code into a comment, it could steal the login cookies of anyone viewing the page.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Protect session cookies from JavaScript access",
        "given": "the application uses cookies for session management",
        "when": "any page is served to a user",
        "then": "set HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict flags on all session cookies"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Phishing via legitimate-looking links in comments",
      "scenario": "Attacker posts comment with link that appears to point to legitimate site but actually redirects to phishing page (e.g., [Check your order](http://evil.com)). Users click link, land on fake login page mimicking the real site, and enter credentials.",
      "component": "comment input form",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-601"],
      "plainLanguage": "Attackers could post links that look safe but redirect users to fake sites designed to steal their passwords.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Mark external links and warn users",
        "given": "a comment contains a hyperlink",
        "when": "the link points to an external domain",
        "then": "add rel='nofollow noopener noreferrer', visual indicator (icon), and optionally show interstitial warning before redirect"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "User tracking via embedded image pixels",
      "scenario": "Attacker posts comment with 1x1 transparent image hosted on their server. Every time someone views the product page, their browser loads the image, sending IP address, user agent, and timestamp to attacker's server, enabling user profiling and tracking.",
      "component": "image handler",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" },
        { "quote": "rendered for every visitor" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.3.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "Hidden tiny images in comments could track everyone who views the page and report their activity to outsiders.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Proxy external images or restrict to trusted hosts",
        "given": "a comment contains an embedded image",
        "when": "the image URL points to external domain",
        "then": "either proxy the image through your server (stripping referrer) or only allow images from approved CDN/upload service"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "SQL injection in comment storage",
      "scenario": "Attacker crafts comment content with SQL injection payload (e.g., '; DROP TABLE comments; --). If comment text is inserted into database query without parameterization, the payload executes, corrupting or deleting database contents.",
      "component": "comment storage",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Comments are stored in the comments database" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-89"],
      "plainLanguage": "Specially crafted comment text could break into the database and delete or modify all comments and other data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Use parameterized queries for all database operations",
        "given": "the application stores comment data in the database",
        "when": "inserting, updating, or querying comments",
        "then": "use prepared statements or ORM with parameterized queries; never concatenate user input into SQL strings"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "CSRF forcing users to post unwanted comments",
      "scenario": "Attacker tricks logged-in user into visiting attacker's page containing hidden form that auto-submits POST request to comment endpoint. If no CSRF protection exists, the victim's session is used to post attacker's comment without victim's knowledge.",
      "component": "comment input form",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.2.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-352"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker could make logged-in users unknowingly post comments by tricking them into visiting a malicious page.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Implement CSRF protection on comment submission",
        "given": "a user is logged in",
        "when": "submitting a new comment",
        "then": "validate a CSRF token (synchronized token pattern or double-submit cookie) on the server before accepting the comment"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Comment spam overwhelming database and page rendering",
      "scenario": "Attacker writes script to rapidly post hundreds or thousands of comments on product pages. Comments fill database storage, slow down page loads as server processes many comments for rendering, and bury legitimate content making products unusable.",
      "component": "comment storage",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "Attackers could flood product pages with thousands of automated comments, making them slow or unusable.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Implement rate limiting on comment submission",
        "given": "a user attempts to post comments",
        "when": "tracking posts per user per time window",
        "then": "limit to reasonable threshold (e.g., 10 comments per hour per user) and return 429 status when exceeded"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Extremely large comments consuming memory and bandwidth",
      "scenario": "Attacker posts comments with tens of thousands of characters or massive images. Storing and retrieving these consumes excessive database space, memory when loading pages, and bandwidth when serving to visitors, degrading performance for all users.",
      "component": "comment input form",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.1.1", "V5.2.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-400"],
      "plainLanguage": "Users could post extremely long comments or huge images that slow down the site for everyone.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce maximum size limits on comments and images",
        "given": "a user submits a comment",
        "when": "validating the submission",
        "then": "reject if text exceeds reasonable length (e.g., 5000 chars), images exceed size limit (e.g., 5MB), or total comment size exceeds threshold"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Unauthorized comment deletion by non-moderators",
      "scenario": "Attacker discovers delete endpoint (e.g., /comments/{id}/delete) lacks proper authorization checks. By crafting requests with different comment IDs, attacker deletes other users' comments or even moderator comments, censoring content.",
      "component": "admin moderation interface",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1", "V4.1.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-862"],
      "plainLanguage": "Users might be able to delete other people's comments if the deletion feature doesn't properly check who's allowed to delete.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Verify moderator role before comment deletion",
        "given": "a deletion request is received for a comment",
        "when": "processing the deletion",
        "then": "verify the requesting user has moderator role before allowing deletion; return 403 otherwise"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Missing audit logs for comment actions",
      "scenario": "Attacker posts offensive or illegal content in comments. When investigated, there's no record of who posted it, when, or from what IP address. Attacker denies responsibility. Similarly, if moderator maliciously deletes legitimate comments, no audit trail exists.",
      "component": "comment storage",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" },
        { "quote": "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.1", "V7.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Without logs showing who posted or deleted comments, it's impossible to investigate abuse or hold people accountable.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Log all comment creation and deletion events",
        "given": "a comment is created or deleted",
        "when": "the action completes successfully",
        "then": "write immutable audit log entry with timestamp, user ID, action, comment ID, IP address, and user agent"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "HTML injection breaking page layout via unclosed tags",
      "scenario": "Attacker posts comment with unclosed HTML tags like <div><div><div>... or extreme nesting. When rendered, it breaks the product page layout, making content below the comment invisible or unusable, degrading experience for all visitors.",
      "component": "rich text parser",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" },
        { "quote": "rendered for every visitor" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79"],
      "plainLanguage": "Malformed HTML in comments could break the page layout, making the product page unreadable.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Parse and sanitize HTML structure before rendering",
        "given": "a comment contains HTML markup",
        "when": "preparing to display it",
        "then": "parse with HTML sanitizer library that auto-closes tags, limits nesting depth, and removes malformed structures"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Sensitive error messages revealing system information",
      "scenario": "When rich-text parsing fails or database errors occur, application displays detailed error messages including stack traces, database schema details, or file paths. Attacker uses this information to refine attacks against specific database version or framework vulnerabilities.",
      "component": "product page renderer",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Comments are stored in the comments database and rendered" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.4.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-209"],
      "plainLanguage": "Error messages could leak details about the system that help attackers find vulnerabilities.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Show generic error messages to users",
        "given": "an error occurs during comment processing or rendering",
        "when": "returning response to user",
        "then": "display generic error message ('Unable to process comment'); log detailed error server-side only"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Algorithmic complexity attack via nested formatting",
      "scenario": "Attacker posts comment with deeply nested formatting tags (bold within italic within underline, repeated 100+ times). Parsing and rendering this causes exponential processing time, consuming CPU and hanging the page renderer, making product pages slow or timeout for all users.",
      "component": "rich text parser",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-407"],
      "plainLanguage": "Extremely complex formatting in comments could make the server work so hard it slows down or crashes.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Limit parsing complexity and nesting depth",
        "given": "parsing rich-text comment content",
        "when": "encountering nested formatting tags",
        "then": "enforce maximum nesting depth (e.g., 10 levels) and timeout parsing after reasonable duration (e.g., 100ms)"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Markdown injection enabling XSS via loose parser",
      "scenario": "If using Markdown for rich text, attacker exploits parser vulnerabilities by using raw HTML passthrough, javascript: URLs in links, or data: URIs in images. These bypass Markdown syntax to inject executable code that runs when rendered.",
      "component": "rich text parser",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79"],
      "plainLanguage": "If Markdown is used, attackers could sneak malicious code through special Markdown features that allow raw HTML.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Configure Markdown parser in safe mode",
        "given": "using Markdown for rich-text formatting",
        "when": "parsing comment content",
        "then": "disable raw HTML passthrough, block javascript: and data: URI schemes, and use library with auto-escaping (e.g., marked.js with sanitize: true)"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

This threat model identifies **15 security threats** across all STRIDE categories for the rich-text comments feature, with the most critical being XSS attacks that could affect all visitors and compromise moderator accounts. Each threat includes verbatim evidence from the provided context, OWASP ASVS and CWE mappings, and actionable security requirements.
